openssl rsa -inform DER -pubin -in rsa_pub.der -out rsa_pub.pem

Sign:

pkcs11-tool \
  --sign \
  --id 1 \
  --pin 648219 \
  --mechanism RSA-PKCS \
  -i data \
  -o data.sig

Verify:

openssl dgst -sha256 -verify rsa_pub.pem -signature data.sig data

Warning

RSA-PKCS is widely interoperable but not the first choice for new designs. Prefer RSA-PSS where your tooling supports it.

docs.title: ECDSA signature flow
docs.text:
Export the public key:

pkcs11-tool --read-object --type pubkey --id 11 --output-file ec_pub.der
openssl ec -inform DER -pubin -in ec_pub.der -out ec_pub.pem

Sign:

pkcs11-tool \
  --sign \
  --id 11 \
  --pin 648219 \
  --mechanism ECDSA \
  -i data \
  -o data.sig

Verify:

openssl dgst -sha256 -verify ec_pub.pem -signature data.sig data

docs.title: What to watch for
docs.text:
• host tools differ on whether hashing is implicit or explicit
  • some mechanisms exist in firmware but are awkward in generic CLI tooling
  • signature success proves the session, PIN, and key object are all aligned correctly

For this reason, sign-and-verify is a useful diagnostic workflow after provisioning.

docs.title: Store data
docs.text: Pico HSM can store non-key data objects alongside cryptographic keys. Use this for small supporting data, since the device is not designed as a general object store.

docs.title: Typical use cases
docs.text:
Reasonable uses include:

  • certificates
  • small metadata blobs
  • application-bound configuration
  • auxiliary secrets tied to the same access-control model

Large arbitrary file storage is not the intended design target.

docs.title: Write a data object
docs.text:
echo "This is a test data" > data.bin

pkcs11-tool \
  --write-object data.bin \
  --type data \
  --id 30 \
  --label my-data \
  --pin 648219

docs.title: List data objects
docs.text:
pkcs11-tool \
  --list-objects \
  --type data \
  --pin 648219

docs.title: Read a data object
docs.text:
pkcs11-tool \
  --read-object \
  --type data \
  --id 30 \
  --output-file read-data.bin \
  --pin 648219

docs.title: Delete a data object
docs.text:
pkcs11-tool \
  --delete-object \
  --type data \
  --id 30 \
  --pin 648219

docs.title: Practical caution
docs.text:
Data objects inherit the management complexity of the HSM:

  • you still need the right session and PIN context
  • object identifiers need discipline
  • restore and migration expectations should be documented up front

Use data objects deliberately and keep their identifiers, access rules, and recovery expectations documented.

docs.title: PicoKey App
docs.text:
PicoKey App is the desktop application for managing PicoKeys devices.

The current release is PicoKey App 3.0.

Use it to:

  • Device detection
  • Device configuration and commissioning
  • Security-related settings (firmware-dependent)
  • FIDO management (passkeys, accounts, and slots)
  • OpenPGP management (OpenPGP card and PIV slots)
  • App settings
  • License and board registration

PicoKey App communicates with the device over USB and shows the features supported by its installed firmware.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Home
  • Configuration
  • About and diagnostics
  • License and registration

docs.title: About and diagnostics
docs.text: Use the About section to check application details and open diagnostic tools.

docs.title: About
docs.text: The About tab shows the PicoKey App version and build information.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
The Diagnostics tab provides diagnostic and debug information useful for troubleshooting.

The diagnostics shown depend on the application build and installed firmware.

docs.title: App settings
docs.text: The application-level settings control how PicoKey App communicates with devices and enables certain advanced features.

docs.title: Available readers
docs.text:
Choose the smart-card or USB reader interface that PicoKey App should use.

  • The list shows each compatible interface that the app detects.
  • The active reader is highlighted.
  • Click refresh to scan for readers again.

Note

In most cases, the default reader selection is sufficient and should not be changed.

docs.title: Force Rescue Interface
docs.text:
Select this option to use the Rescue Interface instead of the default PC/SC interface.

When enabled:

  • PicoKey App bypasses the standard PC/SC stack and communicates through the Rescue Interface.
  • Use it when PC/SC is unavailable or misconfigured.

Warning

The Rescue Interface provides reduced functionality compared to PC/SC.

docs.title: Patch PC/SC
docs.text:
This option attempts to patch the local pcscd service to improve compatibility with PicoKey devices on some Linux distributions.

When enabled:

  • PicoKey App changes the PC/SC service configuration.
  • This may resolve compatibility issues on some distributions.

Danger

This operation requires root privileges and may affect other smart card devices. Use with caution.

docs.title: Enable Notifications
docs.text:
Choose whether PicoKey App displays notifications when the device processes an event. Known events include:

  • A site is requesting your presence by touching the button.
  • A credential has been created.
  • An assertion succeeds for a specific credential.

Note

Notifications are sent to the Notification Center in macOS, Linux and Windows when PicoKey App is running. Enable PicoKey Agent for background monitoring when the main app is closed.

docs.title: Enable Agent
docs.text:
Enable communication with PicoKey Agent here.

When enabled:

  • This lets the device communicate with the local agent and enables advanced operations.

  • The agent is required for features such as:

  • Device time synchronization

  • Audit or traceability features

  • Notification handling like user presence, credential creation or credential assertion.

Note

PicoKey Agent runs as a background service and must be installed separately.

docs.title: Device status indicators
docs.text:
The bottom of the application shows the device's current status:

  • Device connection status (online/offline)
  • Recovery mode state
  • Current device time

Tip

When the agent is enabled, it updates the device time automatically.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text: The Audit section lets you review command and usage activity recorded by the PicoKey, so you can track operations performed on the device.

docs.title: What Audit provides
docs.text:
The Audit Log lists operations in chronological order and shows:

  • Operation number (#)
  • Event name
  • Object/target when available
  • Result (OK / Fail)
  • Timestamp

The Total operations counter shows how many events have been recorded.

docs.title: Access protection (Audit PIN)
docs.text:
You can protect audit access with a dedicated Audit PIN.

From this panel you can:

  • Unlock protected logs
  • Set the Audit PIN (first-time setup)
  • Change the Audit PIN (after setup)

docs.title: Log actions
docs.text:
Use the panel controls to manage the log:

  • Refresh
  • Export Log
  • Clear Log
  • Reset

docs.title: Event indicators and status flags
docs.text:
Status indicators call out conditions that may affect the log, including:

  • Log truncated
  • Log cleared
  • Firmware changed
  • PIN/log protection enabled
  • Clock not synchronized
  • Write errors while storing log entries

The screenshot shows indicators for Log cleared, Firmware changed, and Log protected.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Before configuring a device, it helps to understand how PicoKey App, firmware, board registration, and commissioning fit together.

docs.title: PicoKey App vs firmware
docs.text: PicoKeys has two layers: the desktop application and the firmware on the device.

docs.title: PicoKey App (desktop application)
docs.text:
PicoKey App is the management interface.

PicoKey App handles the management work:

  • It detects devices and displays device and firmware information.
  • It configures and commissions devices, and manages licenses and board registration.
  • It also provides diagnostic and troubleshooting tools.

Note

PicoKey App does not implement cryptographic functionality.

docs.title: Firmware (device functionality)
docs.text:
The installed firmware defines what the device does.

Each firmware variant provides a different set of functions, for example:

  • Pico HSM provides hardware security module features.
  • Pico FIDO provides FIDO2 and WebAuthn authentication.
  • Pico OpenPGP provides OpenPGP smart-card functions.

Note

The same PicoKey App interface is used regardless of the installed firmware.

docs.title: Device, board, and firmware
docs.text: The words device, board, and firmware refer to different parts of the setup.

docs.title: Device
docs.text:
A device is the physical PicoKeys unit connected over USB.

It has:

  • A unique serial number
  • A hardware platform
  • A specific board model

docs.title: Board
docs.text:
A board identifies the exact hardware variant.

PicoKey App uses this information to:

  • Apply correct configuration
  • Bind a license to compatible hardware
  • Ensure firmware compatibility

Danger

Board selection is irreversible once the board is registered.

docs.title: Firmware
docs.text:
The firmware is the software that runs on the device.

It determines:

  • Supported features
  • Available security options
  • Operational behavior

Changing firmware may change device capabilities without changing the hardware.

docs.title: License vs board registration
docs.text: Licensing has two steps, and installing the license does not register a board.

docs.title: License installation
docs.text:
When you install a license:

  • The license data is stored locally
  • No device is modified yet

Note

Installing a license alone does not enable any device functionality.

docs.title: Board registration
docs.text:
When you register a board:

  • Binding a license to a specific board
  • Making the license effective for that device

Danger

Board registration is irreversible.

Once a license is bound to a board, it cannot be transferred or modified.

docs.title: Commissioning
docs.text:
Commissioning finalizes device setup by applying configuration and writing persistent state.

It typically:

  • Applies configuration settings
  • Writes persistent state to the device
  • Prepares the device for normal operation

You normally commission the device after:

  • Firmware installation
  • Board registration

Warning

Commissioning modifies persistent device state.

docs.title: Connection modes
docs.text: A PicoKeys device can appear in different connection modes.

docs.title: RESCUE / BOOTSEL mode
docs.text:
Use this mode for:

  • Initial setup
  • Firmware updates
  • Recovery operations

Note

For new or freshly flashed devices, RESCUE mode is expected.

docs.title: Normal operation mode
docs.text:
In normal mode:

  • The device runs the installed firmware
  • Features exposed depend on the firmware variant

docs.title: Irreversible actions
docs.text:
Some PicoKeys actions cannot be undone. These include:

Examples include:

  • Selecting and registering a board type
  • Binding a license to a board
  • Certain commissioning operations

Danger

Always double-check irreversible actions before confirming.

docs.title: Responsibility model
docs.text:
PicoKeys follows a user-controlled model, where:

  • The user explicitly selects actions
  • PicoKey App does not auto-correct critical decisions
  • Irreversible operations require explicit confirmation

Note

This model prioritizes transparency and user control over automation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Use the Configuration section to customize and commission the device.

docs.title: Vendor / USB identity
docs.text:
Choose how the device identifies itself over USB here.

  • Vendor preset Select a predefined USB identity. The default is PicoKeys.

  • Custom VID:PID (hex) Enter a custom USB Vendor ID and Product ID.

Note

Changing USB identifiers affects how the device is recognized by the operating system. USB Product String is modified according to the vendor presets.

docs.title: Timeouts & LED
docs.text:
This section controls user-interaction timing and the LED.

  • Presence button timeout (s) sets how long a presence-confirmation action waits.

  • LED brightness sets the LED intensity on a scale from 0 to 15.

  • LED dimmable enables brightness control.

  • Power cycle on reset forces a power cycle when the device resets.

  • LED steady (no blink) disables LED blinking patterns.

The installed firmware determines which options are available.

docs.title: Advanced options
docs.text:
• Enable secp256k1 enables this elliptic curve when the firmware supports it.

Note

Some old Android devices do not support this curve. Enabling it will make the device non-detectable.

docs.title: Commission device
docs.text:
Click Commission device to apply the selected configuration and provision the device.

A status message indicates the result of the operation.

Warning

Commissioning modifies persistent device state. Ensure all selected options are correct before proceeding.

docs.title: Registration requirement
docs.text: You must register the board in PicoKey App before commissioning it from this panel.

docs.title: Firmware update
docs.text:
Use PicoKey App to update the firmware running on a PicoKeys device.

Firmware updates modify the software running on the device and may affect available features and behavior.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An update can:

  • install a different firmware variant, such as Pico HSM, Pico FIDO, or Pico OpenPGP;
  • update the current firmware; or
  • recover a device with corrupted or incomplete firmware.

Firmware updates are explicit user actions and are never performed automatically.

docs.title: Supported update modes
docs.text:
Depending on the firmware and device state, PicoKey App may support updates in BOOTSEL / RESCUE mode. New or freshly flashed devices are expected to be in RESCUE mode.

For regular firmware variants, upgrade actions require a registered board in PicoKey App. Rescue firmware update paths may still be available for recovery workflows.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Before you start the update:

  • Ensure the device is connected directly to the computer
  • Avoid USB hubs during the update
  • Close other applications that might access the device
  • Do not disconnect the device during the process

Warning

Interrupting a firmware update may leave the device in a recovery state and require manual intervention.

docs.title: Entering BOOTSEL / RESCUE mode
docs.text:
If the device is not already in BOOTSEL / RESCUE mode:

  1. Go to Home
  2. Click Reboot to BOOTSEL
  3. Wait for the device to reconnect

Once in BOOTSEL / RESCUE mode, PicoKey App should detect the device again.

docs.title: Performing a firmware update
docs.text:
To install an update:

  1. Open the firmware update section in PicoKey App
  2. Use Search to pick the firmware file to be installed (firmware files are usually provided as a binary image)
  3. Click Upgrade to start the update process
  4. Wait until PicoKey App reports completion
  5. Reconnect the device if requested

You can also load a specific firmware file from local disk using the file search/open action in the firmware panel (custom firmware path).

While the update runs:

  • Progress information may be displayed
  • The device may temporarily disconnect and reconnect

docs.title: Wipe entire flash (advanced)
docs.text:
The firmware panel includes an optional Wipe entire flash checkbox.

When enabled, PicoKey App erases flash sectors before writing the new firmware.

Use this only when you explicitly need a full cleanup (for example recovery scenarios), because it removes previous flash contents.

Warning

A full wipe is destructive and may require full reconfiguration or commissioning after flashing.

docs.title: After the update
docs.text:
After the update completes:

  • The device may reboot automatically
  • The reported firmware version should change accordingly
  • Available features in PicoKey App may change depending on the firmware

Then:

  • Return to Home
  • Verify firmware version and device status
  • Perform commissioning if required by the new firmware

docs.title: Firmware update and configuration
docs.text:
Installing a different firmware may:

  • Reset some configuration settings
  • Require re-commissioning
  • Change available configuration or security options

Note

Firmware functionality is defined by the installed firmware, not by PicoKey App itself.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
If an update fails:

  • Do not unplug the device immediately
  • Follow any instructions shown by PicoKey App
  • If the device enters BOOTSEL / RESCUE mode, retry the update

If recovery is not possible or behavior is unclear, open a ticket at:

https://github.com/polhenarejos/picokeyapp/issues

Include:

  • PicoKey App version
  • Firmware version (if known)
  • Device platform and board model
  • A description of what happened and at which step

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• Firmware updates are explicit and user-controlled
  • PicoKey App does not automatically select or install firmware
  • Always verify that you are installing the correct firmware variant for your device

docs.title: First-time use
docs.text: The first time you use PicoKey App with a new device, complete the steps below. Some actions are irreversible, so check each selection before continuing.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
You will need to:

  1. Install a valid license
  2. Connect a compatible PicoKeys device
  3. Select the correct board type
  4. Register the board
  5. Commission the device

Some of these steps cannot be undone.

docs.title: Step 1: Install a license
docs.text:
Before a device can be registered, a valid license must be installed.

  1. Open About → License
  2. If no license is installed, the status will show Not registered
  3. Click Register License
  4. Enter or import your license
  5. Confirm that the license is accepted

After installing the license:

  • The license is installed locally
  • No device is registered yet

docs.title: Step 2: Connect the device
docs.text:
1. Plug the PicoKeys device into a USB port
  2. Use a direct USB connection whenever possible
  3. Launch PicoKey App if it is not already running

Go to Home and verify that:

  • The device is detected
  • A green Device detected indicator is shown

If the device is not detected:

  • Try a different USB cable or port
  • Close other applications that may be accessing the device
  • Reconnect the device and restart PicoKey App

docs.title: Step 3: Select the board type (mandatory)
docs.text:
Before registering the board, you must explicitly select the correct board type.

You must choose the board type yourself before registering it.

  • The board type defines the hardware variant associated with the license
  • PicoKey App cannot automatically infer the correct board in all cases
  • The user is responsible for selecting the correct option

Warning

Once the board type is selected and the board is registered, the board type cannot be changed.

Info

Do not attempt to register the board in BOOTSEL mode. Proceed with a PicoKey firmware running normally.

docs.title: Step 4: Register the board
docs.text:
After selecting the board type:

  1. Go to About → License
  2. Select the target board
  3. Click Register Board
  4. Wait for confirmation

After registration:

  • The license is bound to the selected board
  • The board status changes to Registered

This license-to-board binding cannot be undone.

docs.title: Step 5: Commission the device
docs.text:
After board registration, the device must be commissioned.

  1. Go to Configuration
  2. Review the available configuration options
  3. Click Commission device
  4. Wait for the confirmation message

Commissioning then:

  • Applies the selected configuration
  • Writes persistent state to the device
  • Prepares the device for normal operation

docs.title: If your board is not listed
docs.text:
If your board model does not appear in the board selection list:

  • Do not proceed
  • Do not select a different or “similar” board

Instead, open a support ticket at:

https://github.com/polhenarejos/picokeyapp/issues

Include:

  • The exact board model
  • The version
  • The firmware version running on the device
  • Any relevant screenshots or logs

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Before you finish, confirm that:

  • Installing a license is mandatory
  • The board type must be selected manually by the user
  • Board selection is irreversible
  • Commissioning finalizes the setup
  • If the correct board is not listed, open a ticket before continuing

docs.title: Home
docs.text: The Home section shows an overview of the connected device.

docs.title: Device detection
docs.text:
When PicoKey App detects a device, it shows:

  • Type: device family (e.g. PICOKEY)
  • Connection: current connection mode (e.g. RESCUE)
  • Product: firmware-reported product type
  • Platform: MCU platform (e.g. RP2350)
  • Version: firmware version
  • Serial number: unique device identifier
  • Board status: registration state (Registered / Not registered)
  • Board model: hardware model identifier

The green Device detected indicator confirms that the app can communicate with the device.

docs.title: Memory information
docs.text:
The Memory Info section reports the device's filesystem usage:

  • Free memory
  • Used memory
  • Total memory
  • Number of files
  • Total filesystem size
  • Firmware size

Use these values to check available space or investigate unusual storage usage.

docs.title: Reboot to BOOTSEL
docs.text:
Click Reboot to BOOTSEL to restart the device in BOOTSEL recovery mode.

Warning

BOOTSEL mode should only be used when required (firmware update or recovery). Interrupting critical operations may require manual recovery.

docs.title: Device status indicators
docs.text:
The bottom of the application shows the device's current status:

  • Device connection status (online/offline)
  • Recovery mode state
  • Current device time

Tip

When the agent is enabled, it updates the device time automatically.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Follow the steps for your operating system to install PicoKey App.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
Download PicoKey App from the official downloads page.

Purchase a license to access the download. After your purchase, a download link will arrive by email; the Downloads page provides builds for Windows, Linux, and macOS, along with the corresponding license file.

Note

Always download PicoKey App from official sources to avoid tampered binaries.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
1. Download the .exe portable build.
  2. No installer is required. Just put the app in the desired folder.
  3. Launch PicoKey App from the Start menu.

docs.title: Windows driver notes
docs.text:
PicoKey App uses standard USB drivers where possible. If your device is not detected, go to:

  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
1. Download the .dmg (or .zip) build.
  2. Drag PicoKey App into Applications.
  3. Open PicoKey App.

Tip

If macOS blocks the app, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and allow it to run.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
1. Download the AppImage.
  2. Make it executable: 
    chmod +x PicoKey App.AppImage
  3. Run it: 
    ./PicoKey App.AppImage

Tip

If Linux does not detect the device, you may need to add udev rules or adjust group permissions. See:

  • Troubleshooting

After installation, continue with First steps to set up the device.

docs.title: License and registration
docs.text: Use the License section to install licenses and register boards.

docs.title: Unregistered state
docs.text:
Without an installed license:

  • The status shows Not registered
  • The Register License button is available

docs.title: Registered state
docs.text:
After you install a license:

  • The registered user is displayed
  • The target board can be selected
  • The Register Board button binds the license to the device

Note

The number of boards you can register depends on the seats included with your licenses. You can add seats by purchasing more licenses with the same email address.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Follow this first-time workflow to connect and commission a device with PicoKey App. It starts from a device with no prior configuration.

docs.title: Step 1: Connect the device
docs.text:
1. Plug the PicoKeys device into a USB port.
  2. Use a direct USB connection whenever possible (avoid hubs during initial setup).
  3. Launch PicoKey App.

PicoKey App should detect the device within a few seconds.

docs.title: Step 2: Verify device detection
docs.text:
Go to Home.

When detection succeeds, the green Device detected indicator appears with details such as:

  • Platform (e.g. RP2350)
  • Firmware version
  • Serial number
  • Board model
  • Board status (Registered / Not registered)

If the device is not detected:

  • Try a different USB port or cable
  • Close other applications that might be accessing the device
  • Reconnect the device and restart PicoKey App

docs.title: Step 3: Check connection mode
docs.text:
In the Home section, check the Connection field.

Typical values include:

  • RESCUE: the device is in recovery or commissioning mode.
  • Other values depending on the installed firmware

For a new or freshly flashed device, RESCUE mode is expected.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure the device
docs.text:
Go to Configuration.

Review the available options:

  • USB identity (Vendor preset, VID:PID, Product string)
  • Timeouts and LED behavior
  • Advanced options (if supported)

Review these options and change any settings you need.

Note

Available options depend on the installed firmware. Unsupported options may have no effect.

docs.title: Step 5: Commission the device
docs.text:
Still in Configuration, click Commission device.

Commissioning applies your selections, provisions the device, and writes persistent state to it.

  • Applies the selected configuration
  • Provisions the device
  • Writes persistent state to the device

Wait for a success message, such as Commissioned successfully.

Warning

Commissioning modifies persistent device state. Ensure all settings are correct before proceeding.

docs.title: Step 6: (Optional) Register a license
docs.text:
Go to About → License.

If the device is not registered:

  1. Click Register License
  2. Enter or load your license information
  3. If required, select the target board
  4. Click Register Board

Once completed, the board status should change to Registered.

docs.title: Step 7: Verify final status
docs.text:
Return to Home and verify:

  • Device is detected
  • Board status is correct
  • No error messages are displayed

The device is now ready to use with its installed firmware.

docs.title: What’s next?
docs.text:
PicoKey App presents the same interface across firmware variants. Choose the guide for your installed firmware:

  • Pico HSM: cryptographic operations and PKCS#11 usage.
  • Pico FIDO: FIDO2 and WebAuthn authentication.
  • Pico OpenPGP: OpenPGP smart-card workflows.

docs.text: This page records notable PicoKey App features covered by these documents.
